exercises.title: Priorities 1 — MoSCoW
exercises.problemHtml:
MoSCoW: Must — the release fails without it; Should — important, painful to omit, but there is a workaround; Could — nice to have, first to be cut; Won’t (this time) — explicitly out of scope for now, recorded. Classify the requirements for release 1 of a food-delivery app.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Priorities 3 — why prioritise, and the games
exercises.problemHtml:
Prioritisation delivers the most value earliest, manages scope against fixed deadlines and attacks high-risk items early. A common game: every stakeholder marks their request "Must". Counter it: cap the Musts (e.g. ≤ 60% of the effort), require each Must to trace to a business objective, and make trade-offs visible ("if this is a Must, which Must drops?").

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

Yêu cầu

  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

# Priorities 3 — why prioritise, and the games — answer key

1. 85% of the requirements are Must. What do you do?85% yêu cầu là Must. Làm gì?
   Answer: c) Cap the Musts and ask which Must drops for each new Must; trace Musts to objectives
   Make trade-offs explicit.VI: Làm đánh đổi minh bạch.

2. Why attack high-risk items early?Vì sao xử lý mục rủi ro cao sớm?
   Answer: b) So there is still time to react if they fail
   Late failures leave no room.VI: Thất bại muộn không còn đường lùi.

3. Who should decide priorities?Ai quyết định ưu tiên?
   Answer: d) Customer representatives together with the team, which estimates cost and risk
   Value from customers, cost and risk from the team.VI: Giá trị từ khách, chi phí và rủi ro từ đội.

exercises.title: Priorities 2 — rank by value ÷ (cost + risk)
exercises.problemHtml:
Lesson 10.1 scores each feature 1–9 on value (higher is better), cost and risk (higher is worse), and computes priority = value / (cost + risk). Write function rank(features) returning a new array of { id, priority } sorted by priority (highest first), priority rounded to 2 decimals. Ties keep the input order. Features with any score outside 1–9 are left out. Do not modify the input.

Requirements

  • rank(FEATURES) ⇒ F1 1.8, F2 1, F4 1, F3 0.24.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Chấm mỗi tính năng 1–9 theo value, cost, risk; priority = value / (cost + risk). Viết rank(features) trả mảng mới { id, priority } giảm dần, làm tròn 2 chữ số; hoà giữ thứ tự đầu vào; bỏ tính năng có điểm ngoài 1–9; không sửa đầu vào.

Yêu cầu

  • rank(FEATURES) ⇒ F1 1.8, F2 1, F4 1, F3 0.24.
hintsJson: Lọc trước, rồi tính, rồi sắp; giữ chỉ số gốc để phá hoà.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: The formula surfaces quick wins (high value, low cost and risk). It turns a political argument into a defensible ranking — but the numbers are relative estimates; the conversation they provoke matters as much as the result.
